parts.name: nut_plate
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted: the T8 brass nut z_nut rides lead screw leadscrew. Its 22 mm flange is under this 6.35 mm plate, which is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_rear (two M5 from below into T-nuts), and its 10.2 mm barrel goes up through the plate's 16.6 mm hole. The carrier's weight rests on the flange, so when the screw turns the nut climbs it and lifts the plate, the square, the deck and the bed. The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2.8 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it. The three nut plates are one shape, as are the three keepers.

The M2.5 pin screw nut_pin_fr (through a 5 mm aluminium sleeve, fixed in the flange) sits in a radial slot in the plate: it stops the nut turning with the screw while letting it float 2.8 mm sideways. The nut is captive: the laser-cut keeper nut_keeper_fr, bolted 0.1 mm under the flange on two M3 through-bolts and spacers, stops the plate lifting off it. The three nut plates are one shape, as are the three keepers.
